il-ag-2026-raoul-kwame.name: Kwame Raoul
il-ag-2026-raoul-kwame.bio: Illinois Attorney General since January 2019; former prosecutor and state legislator.

positions.stance: Prioritizes fighting crime in Illinois and working to "reduce the number of illegal guns on our streets," including through a crime gun tracing platform.
Protected "the fundamental right to abortion" by defending the Reproductive Health Act and protected access to mifepristone.
Seeks to hold social media platforms accountable for "profiting from addictive features" that contribute to young users' declining wellbeing.
Calls protecting children from online predators a top priority and has fought for "tougher sentences for people who abuse or exploit children."
"Committed to ending price gouging" and holding companies, including pharmacy benefit managers, accountable for driving prices up.

il-ag-2026-fioretti-robert.name: Robert W. Fioretti
il-ag-2026-fioretti-robert.bio: Attorney and former Chicago 2nd Ward alderman; former Special Assistant Attorney General of Illinois.

positions.stance: Committed to "protecting consumers and families from fraud, scams, and corporate abuse."
Committed to "holding government accountable by exposing corruption and ensuring transparency at all levels."
Committed to "safeguarding civil rights so every Illinoisan has equal protection under the law."
Committed to "supporting local law enforcement, fighting gun violence, and addressing the root causes of crime."
Committed to "enforcing laws that guarantee equal access and fair treatment for students and families."

il-sos-2026-giannoulias-alexi.name: Alexi Giannoulias
il-sos-2026-giannoulias-alexi.bio: Illinois Secretary of State, elected in 2022; former Illinois State Treasurer.

positions.stance: Committed to "advancing initiatives that will expand voter rights and make voting easier and more convenient."
Supports toughening ethics laws, saying Illinoisans are "sick and tired of the corruption and scandals" in the state.
Supports changing how the Secretary of State's office operates and delivers services "to improve the customer experience."
Plans "a universal License to Read program to improve access to libraries" and more digital services online.
Would push the state to provide "ex-offenders with valid state identification cards before their release from prison."

il-sos-2026-harris-diane.name: Diane M. Harris
il-sos-2026-harris-diane.bio: Retired liability representative at ComEd and small business owner; Joliet Junior College trustee.

positions.stance: Would "advocate for safer smarter rules of the roads protecting families safety and young drivers."
Would "expedite customer service in person and remote services" at the Secretary of State's office.
Would "clean up the voter rolls and promote election integrity during all registrations."
Would "strengthen cybersecurity to protect against fraud and protect your personal information."
Would "deliver modern, innovative services that are faster, fairer, and more accessible to all Illinoisans."

il-comp-2026-croke-margaret.name: Margaret Croke
il-comp-2026-croke-margaret.bio: Illinois state representative and chair of the House Financial Institutions committee.

positions.stance: Supports "true budget-to-billing transparency," with software showing public dollars from the state budget line item to payment.
Would modernize the Comptroller's systems and use predictive modeling "to enhance efficiency and reduce fraud and waste."
Supports balanced budgets that invest in communities and "pay down the backlog of bills."
Would enforce the Prevailing Wage Act "by withholding payments to employers who underpay their workers and break the law."

il-comp-2026-drew-bryan.name: Bryan Drew
il-comp-2026-drew-bryan.bio: Attorney who has run his own Southern Illinois law firm for over 25 years and co-owner of a family café in Benton.

positions.stance: Wants to "stop government waste so we can lower costs for working families" by "forcing government to live within its means."
Wants to be an independent watchdog who will "hold politicians accountable for how they spend our tax dollars."
Would present state spending data "in an easily understandable way that's user-friendly" so taxpayers can see where their dollars go.

il-treas-2026-frerichs-michael.name: Michael W. Frerichs
il-treas-2026-frerichs-michael.bio: Illinois State Treasurer since 2015, elected in 2014 and re-elected in 2018 and 2022.

positions.stance: Prioritizes "putting more money back in your pocket," citing more than $2.6 billion in missing money returned to Illinoisans.
Prioritizes "helping families build a secure financial future" through college savings and workplace retirement savings programs.
Prioritizes "investing in Illinois jobs, housing, and communities," including affordable housing and financing for small businesses and family farms.

il-treas-2026-solomon-max.name: Max Solomon
il-treas-2026-solomon-max.bio: Attorney practicing in Illinois and Indiana and adjunct professor of political science and law at South Suburban Community College.

positions.stance: Proposes "a real-time public dashboard so Illinois taxpayers always know where their money is — and how it's growing."
Would modernize the state's investment strategy "to maximize returns while maintaining fiduciary responsibility."
Would strengthen the Bright Start and Bright Directions college savings programs.
Would direct "state deposits to community banks and credit unions across all 102 counties."

ga-sos-2026-fleming-tim.name: Tim Fleming
ga-sos-2026-fleming-tim.bio: Georgia state representative for House District 114 and small business owner; former Chief of Staff to Governor Brian Kemp and Deputy Secretary of State.

positions.stance: Would "ensure our elections are secure, accessible, fair, and trusted."
Would "streamline professional licensing to get Georgians licensed faster."
Would "cut the red tape holding small businesses back."
Would "protect voter ID and champion election transparency."
Would "enhance technology to better serve Georgians."

ga-sos-2026-reynolds-penny.name: Penny Brown Reynolds
ga-sos-2026-reynolds-penny.bio: Former Fulton County judge and Executive Counsel to a Georgia governor; former acting USDA Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights.

positions.stance: Would expand early voting sites and strengthen absentee ballot access with "convenient drop boxes" for "free, fair, and accessible elections."
Would "streamline business formation processes" and launch a "Business Access Georgia" digital dashboard for entrepreneurs.
Would reduce license processing wait times and offer priority processing for nurses, teachers, contractors, and social workers.
Would partner with law enforcement and nonprofits to launch a "Statewide Fraud Protection Campaign" protecting seniors from exploitation.
Would "establish a public data portal that tracks performance metrics on elections, business filings, and licenses."

ga-ag-2026-strickland-brian.name: Brian Strickland
ga-ag-2026-strickland-brian.bio: Georgia state senator and Chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee; attorney.

positions.stance: Would go after "violent crime, gangs, dangerous counterfeit drugs, human trafficking, and the criminal networks that cross city and county lines."
Prioritizes "protecting seniors, foster children, families with special needs, and consumers from abuse, scams, and fraud."
"The same law should apply to everyone, regardless of party, wealth, influence, or connections."
Prioritizes "protecting clean water, working farms, and healthy communities while supporting responsible growth."

ga-ag-2026-miller-tanya.name: Tanya Miller
ga-ag-2026-miller-tanya.bio: Georgia state representative, civil rights attorney, and former prosecutor.

positions.stance: Would "target and dismantle violent criminal networks, human trafficking rings" and those trafficking illegal guns and fentanyl into Georgia.
Would investigate the grocery supply chain and "challenge unfair and unjustified rate hikes from power and utility monopolies."
Would "establish a Small Business Protection Unit" in the Attorney General's office and challenge monopolistic practices.
Would "safeguard our most fundamental right—the right to vote" and protect Georgians' privacy from government intrusion and corporate overreach.
Would "aggressively prosecute robocall operations, identity thieves and online scammers" and fight predatory lending.

ga-agr-2026-harper-tyler.name: Tyler Harper
ga-agr-2026-harper-tyler.bio: Georgia's Agriculture Commissioner and a seventh-generation farmer and small business owner.

positions.stance: Fighting "corporate consolidation" and working "to restore competition in the agriculture industry and food supply chain" to lower grocery costs.
Believes data centers should "pay 100% of the infrastructure and utility costs" and never be forced on a community that does not want one.
Says Georgia farmers "have a profitability problem"; working to block food industry mergers and expand market access for farmers.
Wants to put more Georgia Grown food in school lunchrooms, building on the more than 25% of schools now serving it.
Will pursue "a farmers-first agenda that prioritizes new funding and additional support for farms and agribusiness" and expand Georgia Grown.

ga-agr-2026-juhan-arnold-katherine.name: Katherine E. Juhan-Arnold
ga-agr-2026-juhan-arnold-katherine.bio: Farmer and founder of Baby Katie's Pharm & Kitchen, working in community agriculture and farm-to-school initiatives.

positions.stance: Will "support policies that strengthen economic growth, supply chains, rural prosperity" for Georgia's agricultural businesses.
Will support expanded market access, address rising input costs, and develop programs that support "generational transition" on farms.
Will "support sustainable forestry markets, strengthen conservation partnerships, improve wildfire coordination" and protect forestry jobs.
Will support trade missions, "grow the Georgia Grown brand," and support value-added production in the state.
Will support farm-to-school programs, regional food hubs, and institutional procurement while strengthening international trade relationships.

ga-ins-2026-king-john.name: John King
ga-ins-2026-king-john.bio: Georgia Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner; retired major general and former police chief.

positions.stance: Says his office has recovered "more than $100 MILLION from insurance companies" for Georgia families through consumer complaints.
"Fighting to increase the maximum initial fines allowed" against insurance companies that take advantage of Georgians.
Helped deliver tort reform and is "focused on making sure insurance companies follow through on their promise to lower rates."
Supports the state-run Georgia Access exchange that took Georgia "out of Obamacare," citing more providers and record enrollment.
As state fire marshal, has expanded partnerships with law enforcement and first responders and tripled the number of arson K-9s.

ga-ins-2026-waites-keisha.name: Keisha Sean Waites
ga-ins-2026-waites-keisha.bio: Former three-term Georgia state representative and Atlanta City Council member; former FEMA and SBA disaster-recovery staff.

positions.stance: Proposes a "Rate Freeze Initiative," "aggressively reviewing and challenging unjustified rate hikes for auto and home insurance."
Calls to "End Zip Code and Credit Score Discrimination" in insurance.
Would create "a dedicated task force to protect seniors and vulnerable families from predatory insurance scams."

ga-supt-2026-woods-richard.name: Richard Woods
ga-supt-2026-woods-richard.bio: Georgia State School Superintendent for over 10 years; former classroom teacher, principal, and curriculum director.

positions.stance: Supports "getting back to basics in reading & math."
Supports "expanding diploma options for students."
Supports "strengthening personal finance & civics education."
Supports "preparing our students for high demand, high wage careers."
Supports "reducing screen time" and protecting teacher planning time.

ga-supt-2026-powell-lydia.name: Lydia Powell
ga-supt-2026-powell-lydia.bio: Educator with over 26 years of teaching experience, including 11 years in educational leadership.

positions.stance: Calls for "transparent leadership and responsible use of resources," with decisions centered on student outcomes and community trust.
Supports "setting high standards for every student and providing the support needed to reach them."
Seeks "measurable improvements in student achievement, graduation rates, and career readiness" through data-informed decisions.

ga-labor-2026-holmes-barbara.name: Bárbara Rivera Holmes
ga-labor-2026-holmes-barbara.bio: Georgia Labor Commissioner, appointed by Governor Brian Kemp in April 2025.

positions.stance: Strengthening connections between small employers and talent pipelines and "streamlining hiring processes."
Replacing the unemployment system with "a secure, cloud-based platform designed to accelerate claims processing, reduce fraud."
Building partnerships with colleges, workforce boards, and training programs for pathways "into higher-wage, high-demand careers."
Overhauling the claims process "to eliminate backlogs, speed up benefits, and crack down on fraud."
"Advocating for policies that strengthen wages, improve worker protections, and advance economic mobility."

ga-labor-2026-porcher-nikki.name: Nikki Porcher
ga-labor-2026-porcher-nikki.bio: U.S. Air Force veteran, former Georgia public school teacher, and leader of a national nonprofit supporting small businesses.

positions.stance: Supports accessible, affordable child care, saying "families should not have to spend most of their paycheck just to go to work."
Supports "entrepreneurship and workforce growth together" to create stronger local economies.
Prioritizes fair pay and safe workplaces: "When workers are treated with dignity and paid fairly, businesses are stronger."
Says Georgia's workforce systems "should be modern, efficient, and accessible to every community."
Supports "pathways to careers that provide stability, dignity, and growth."

ga-psc3-2026-johnson-fitz.name: Fitz Johnson
ga-psc3-2026-johnson-fitz.bio: Businessman and 21-year U.S. Army veteran; served as Public Service Commissioner from 2021 through December 2025.

positions.stance: Pledges to "protect Georgia ratepayers," saying families and businesses need "affordable, reliable utilities."
Supports "an America First energy agenda that delivers affordability and reliability for every Georgia ratepayer."
Pledges to "hold the line against radical policies."
Pledges to "keep Georgia the #1 state to do business."

ga-psc3-2026-hubbard-peter.name: Peter Hubbard
ga-psc3-2026-hubbard-peter.bio: Georgia Public Service Commissioner since January 2026; former solar developer employee and consumer advocate before the PSC.

positions.stance: Campaigns for "lower utility bills & reliable, clean energy."
Demanded "an independent audit of Georgia Power's profit margin," arguing it is significantly above national averages.
Says building gas power for data centers "instead of clean power will increase the cost of electricity for Georgians."

ga-psc5-2026-tolbert-josh.name: Josh Tolbert
ga-psc5-2026-tolbert-josh.bio: Professional engineer with experience in power generation and industrial facilities.

positions.stance: Would "ensure costs are allocated to those who cause them — not shifted onto ratepayers," including data center-driven costs.
Would "evaluate load forecasts and infrastructure plans for realism and risk" and challenge speculative investments.
Would "ensure Georgia maintains sufficient reserve margins" and support transmission, distribution, and pipeline reliability.
Supports cleaner technologies "only when benefits are measurable and verifiable" and rejects "costly mandates that burden families."

ga-psc5-2026-edwards-shelia.name: Shelia Edwards
ga-psc5-2026-edwards-shelia.bio: Community advocate, journalist, and business owner; former Interim Executive Director of the Georgia House Democratic Caucus.

positions.stance: Running "to fight for affordable electric bills" and ensure Georgia Power "is held accountable for every dollar it asks customers to pay."
Says data centers "must pay the full cost of the infrastructure needed to serve them" rather than residential customers and small businesses.
Says "the public has a right to know who benefits, who pays, and who bears the consequences" of data centers.

mi-sos-2026-gilchrist-garlin.name: Garlin Gilchrist II
mi-sos-2026-gilchrist-garlin.bio: Lieutenant Governor of Michigan; former Microsoft software engineer.

positions.stance: Would "fight for more legislative action that shine a light on dark money in our politics."
Would "modernize licensing and registration by providing smarter, 21st century service."
Would oppose big tech companies and the Trump administration that "want to abuse your personal voter registration information or license-plate data."
Would "hold accountable companies that rip you off when you get your car fixed."

mi-sos-2026-forlini-anthony.name: Anthony G. Forlini
mi-sos-2026-forlini-anthony.bio: Macomb County Clerk; former state representative, township supervisor, and businessman.

positions.stance: Supports voting systems that are "secure, auditable, and protected from avoidable vulnerabilities," including limiting internet exposure in results reporting.
Supports "regular cleanup for deceased voters and outdated records" with documentation and due process safeguards.
Would push for "tools that make records requests more straightforward and timely" and clear explanations of election processes.
Would "enforce election law consistently, fairly and evenly" and refer credible violations to law enforcement when warranted.
Would set "service standards with measurable turnaround expectations" and pursue careful, resident-first modernization.

mi-ag-2026-savit-eli.name: Eli Savit
mi-ag-2026-savit-eli.bio: Washtenaw County Prosecuting Attorney; former civil-rights attorney and public school teacher.

positions.stance: Would work "not just to prosecute serious crime, but to prevent it from happening in the first place."
Would fight "wage theft, payroll fraud, labor trafficking, and unsafe working conditions" and defend workers' right to organize.
Would "litigate to stop price gouging, deceptive practices, and other consumer abuse."
Would ensure every Michigander's rights are protected "regardless of race, sex, religion, sexual orientation, or gender identity."
Would use every tool to protect free speech, due process, and the right "to be free from federal overreach."

mi-ag-2026-lloyd-doug.name: Doug Lloyd
mi-ag-2026-lloyd-doug.bio: Prosecutor for more than 30 years and former president of the Michigan Prosecutors Association.

positions.stance: "I will prosecute criminals fairly, without political favor or bias."
"I will advise lawmakers in crafting strong, commonsense laws for Michigan."
"I will protect your God-given constitutional rights without compromise."
"I will stand firmly against political lawfare and weaponized prosecutions."
"I will root out corruption, stop political overreach, and defend Michigan's sovereignty."

az-sos-2026-fontes-adrian.name: Adrian Fontes
az-sos-2026-fontes-adrian.bio: Arizona Secretary of State, elected in 2022; former Maricopa County Recorder, prosecutor, and U.S. Marine Corps veteran.

az-sos-2026-kolodin-alexander.name: Alexander Kolodin
az-sos-2026-kolodin-alexander.bio: Election lawyer, small business owner, and Arizona state representative for Legislative District 3.

positions.stance: Would "implement robust security protocols to ensure every legal vote is counted accurately."
Would administer elections reflecting voters' choices, "free from bureaucratic overreach or partisan interference."
Would "modernize our election administration to deliver faster reporting without compromising integrity or accuracy."
Says "trust in our elections begins with transparency and accountability" and would bring both to the office.
